title: Larger connectors: which family, and how far
ask: Which plug family should the merged unit connectors use, and should the dash post's leg plugs be merged too?
why:
You asked (chat, 2026-10-14): "we schould consider larger connectors everywhere for consistancy and means less connectors to disconnect when removing things". This picks which plug family the merged connectors use, and how far the merging goes. It decides the crimp tools you buy and what the three unit boards are drawn with before they are ordered.

Where merging helps when something comes out:
- the Control Unit: five plugs already became one (D-582, drawn on a Molex CMC 48 for now);
- the Display Unit: two plugs (6 + 12 conductors) could become one 24-way;
- the CUR: two plugs (12 + 6) could become one 24-way;
- behind the dash, the radar receiver's two receptacles (L3-RDR and the new L3-RCV) could become one 12-way.

The dash post's 16 leg plugs could also become four, one per leg, but legs come off rarely, the power pins there need a third, larger terminal size, and the dash node's plug plate would be redrawn.

What each family costs you:
- Deutsch DT/DTP is what the whole car uses now, and your crimper (P038) is already bought for it.
- Deutsch DRC, the large Deutsch family, uses the same solid contacts: size 16 (13 A) or size 20 (7.5 A), one size per housing. The 24-way right-angle header (DRC13-24PA, size 16) fits the Display Unit and the CUR with no new tool. For the Control Unit, the only size-20 50-way header found is a vertical one. A right-angle 50-way, or a 60- or 70-way, would be needed: confirm. On size-20 pins the three 14 AWG grounds become five 16 AWG ones. Size-20 contacts need a crimper die for size 20 if P038 does not do it.
- Molex CMC mixes 0.64 mm (6 A) and 1.5 mm (12 A) terminals in one housing, which is why the CU fits in 48 ways with no spare. It needs Molex's own crimp tools: about $141 for the small terminals (one listing), and the 1.5 mm tool (Molex 638119000) price was not found. Molex's other CMC tools list at several hundred dollars.

Nothing for the harness is bought yet (A0 is open), and none of the three unit boards is ordered (Y18 waits on this).
options:
(a) Deutsch everywhere: the Control Unit on one Deutsch DRC 50-way or larger header, the Display Unit and the CUR on one DRC 24-way each, the radar receiver's two receptacles merged into one DT 12-way, and the dash post left as it is. One contact system for the whole car and your crimper already bought. It may need a size-20 die. The CU's DRC header must be found in right-angle (confirm), and the CMC rows go.
(b) Molex CMC at the Control Unit only, as D-582 drew it, and Deutsch for everything else with the same merges as (a): Display Unit and CUR on DRC 24, radar on DT 12. It needs two Molex crimp tools (about $141 plus one not priced, likely several hundred), but the CU keeps 12 A large terminals and an exact fit.
(c) As (a), and also the dash post: each leg's 3-5 plugs at the post become one large hybrid housing per leg (16 plugs become 4), with a third, larger terminal size for the 25 A feeds. This is the most consistent, but also the most tools, money and redrawing (the dash node's plug plate, about 170 cavities). Not priced.
(d) Only the Control Unit's one connector (D-582, CMC). Every other plug stays as it is.
recommend: (a), unless no right-angle Deutsch DRC header of 50 ways or more is sold - then (b), whose CMC 48 is known to fit the Control Unit.
stops: Y54 (the Control Unit's header drawn on the carrier), the Display Unit's and the CUR's one-connector rework, the CMC parts P220-P225, and Y18 (the board order) behind them.
